raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Aioli
raw_recipe.description: This creamy aioli is quick and easy to make with mayo, a few garlic cloves, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Perfect as a dip or spread on sandwiches.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make an amazing flavor-packed dipping sauce that you will use over and over again. This delicious garlic aioli makes the ideal dipping sauce for fries, seafood, sandwiches, and vegetables. Lemon juice, garlic, salt, and pepper combine with creamy mayonnaise for a tangy taste that everyone will love. And, with just five ingredients, this quick and easy sauce just might earn a permanent spot in your refrigerator.

review.reviewBody: So much easier than preparing it from scratch and with great results! Loved it, and it was perfect to accompany our crab cakes. I made no changes, nor will I next time.

So very easy & PERFECT just the way it is! However, here are some
minor tips: Don't fear the garlic! Add a bit more if you're feeling a little frisky!
Allow the Aioli to marinate for at least an hour to tame the lemon flavor. I only used 1 tbs. since my partner isn't fond of any heavy lemon flavor. Try some dill & cilantro in it if serving it with fish of any kind. Fresh chives are also great in it!
Add some fresh Basil either in it or on the side if you're one of those wimpy ones that whine about the heavy garlic flavor.
In addition to the black pepper, white pepper can give it that extra kick! Then again, like I said folks, this recipe is perfect just the way it's written! Don't waste your precious time making Garlic Aioli from scratch. Sometimes easy & basic is best!

Fantastic! I made mine in the food processor so that the garlic would be very finely minced. It went very well with my black bean burgers, served as a great dipping sauce for french fries, and I am planning on pairing this with a roasted artichoke tomorrow night.

Very yummy! Hubs said this sauce is a must every time I make sliders. I followed the recipe, but roasted a whole head of garlic instead of using raw (cut tops off, rub with olive oil, wrap tightly with foil and bake at 350 for 45-50 minutes). Also added a pinch of Herbs de Province. Was also great with our oven fries.

Fantastic recipe - I made my own mayonnaise however, as I recently discovered it is very easy & doesn't have to be as complicated. Place an egg in the bottom of a jar, pour in 1 cup of olive oil (or oil of your choice) & add the other ingredients in for flavour, then get a stick blender, place it at the bottom of the jar & start blending, you will see the mayonnaise forming before your eyes. Only takes a few minutes & tastes devine

I found a recipe for Garlic Aoli and made and loved it! I have been unable to get back to that recipe for some reason. (It wasn’t on this website). This one is very close and both were easy. The only change I make to this is to use a half cup of good mayo and a half cup of sour cream, instead of all mayo. The sour cream adds a little tang that we like. The other recipe called for that. Both are great recipes! I forgot to add that we love this with wraps, salmon, beef tenderloin and many other things. I swear that I could eat this with just about anything!

I made this as instructed but roasted, mashed, then diced the garlic before adding to the condiment. (I wanted to roast red pepper anyway.) This was such an easy recipe and really elevated my grilled chicken sandwiches. I will definitely make this again.
Delicious aioli! I agree with other reviewers that it is way too salty. I only added 1/2 tsp and it was still too much. I will add only 1/8-1/4 tsp next time. Otherwise it is perfect!

This is incredible. I make 2 small changes. I halved the recipe (so you can double these additions if you want the full amounts) and added a 1/2 tsp of both paprika, and dried dill. This makes it taste nearly identical to the garlic aioli from Cactus Club Cafe (Canadian chain) and is hands down the best garlic mayo you’ll ever have. It also gives it a nice color!

I made flat breads with grilled steak, fresh mozzarella, roasted bell pepper and cherry tomatoes that I drizzled this sauce on top of after cooking. By itself there was way too much lemon and salt but once it was combined with everything else was good. I will remake it with less of those ingredients and probably try Greek yogurt in place of the mayo.

As written had too much lemon juice. But with this addition we loved it: added 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce, a tsp horseradish, and a Tbsp Dijon mustard. Broke down that overpowering lemon flavor and made for an amazing gourmet burger topping. (We will do it again with our changes absolutely!!!)
It reminds me of my garlic dip I make for dipping potato chips...cream cheese, garlic salt (to taste) and a little milk! So good!

LOVE love love this simple aioli recipe!! We have made this a few times now. The last time we added a bit of truffle oil to make a garlic truffle aioli sauce and it was out of this world. Definitely will be making this again and again! Thank you for sharing.
Very fast and delicious. It's great on turkey burgers!
Great with fried calamari. Was a bit too lemony for my taste so next time I'll add less.
I love this, I use it on a pasta salad, I added about 2 Tbs whole milk to loosen it up add some minced celery and put it in the fridge. Delish!
I add a little bit of Dijon Mustard to this recipe. It gives it a little more zip and is really good on steak, Italian subs tuna or chicken salad and burgers.
Way too wet way too salty this was a disaster. I followed the recipe exactly.
Awesome!! I did double the garlic!!
Superb!
